newsitem.title: MEXICO: Apasco 1996 beats forecast but sets concern.
newsitem.headline: Apasco 1996 beats forecast but sets concern.

text.p: Mexico cement-maker Apasco posted 1996 earnings per share that outstripped expectations but were disappointing in operating terms, analysts said on Monday.

"The report was very good in year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter terms," said Carlos Perezalonso, an equity analyst with ABN Amro Bank in Mexico City. "They posted growth in sales, operating earnings and volumes."
Apasco reported 1996 earnings per share of 3.93 pesos compared with an average forecast of 3.73 pesos by six analysts in a Reuters survey.

"I never thought volumes in Mexico would grow eight percent, year-on-year, in Q4 1996, and neither did I think ready-mixed concrete sales would grow by 23 percent," said Paul Rodriguez, an analyst with Caspian Securities in New York.
Analysts noted that Q4 volumes also were positive on quarter-on-quarter terms.

Sobani Warner of Bear Stearns in New York drew attention in a report to the 28-percent growth in domestic tonnage between Q3 and Q4, "signalling that market share likely rose to 25 percent from 22 percent in Q3."

Nonetheless, analysts said quarter-on-quarter comparisons did not look so good for the company's margins. Apasco's operating margin fell to 20 percent in Q4 from 29 percent in Q3 due to lower prices and higher energy costs.
"Prices definitely came lower than expected, although volumes were in line with expectations, even a little higher," said Eric Linder, an analyst with JP Morgan in New York.
Gordon Lee of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Mexico City said "The market may react negatively; earnings for the (fourth) quarter look disappointing in operating terms."
